authority: Generated executable projection. Edit _validation_registry.json, then run npm run validation:matrix.

lineage_policy.authority: _validation_registry.json is the executable source of truth for validation selection, dependency order, prerequisites, outputs, severity, and mutation boundaries.
lineage_policy.dependency_rule: Dependencies are included recursively and executed in topological order before dependents.
lineage_policy.prerequisite_rule: Missing required files trigger registered prepare_commands. Unregistered preparation is forbidden.
lineage_policy.mutation_rule: Validator commands may write only declared mutates_files. Source roots are hash-checked before and after each validator.
lineage_policy.output_rule: Declared produces_files must exist after a passing validator.

HARD_FAIL.meaning: Direct production, user-safety, evidence, route, workflow, build, or delivery threat; never cosmetic formatting.

STRONG_WARNING.meaning: Material quality, ingestion, indexing, accessibility, or performance degradation.

SOFT_WARNING.meaning: Maintainability, documentation, style, or low-risk quality concern.

INFO.meaning: Metric, observation, historical evidence, or optimization note.

scope_definitions.CONTAINER: Runnable in the standard container without provider credentials.
scope_definitions.LOCAL_ONLY: Requires deployed URL, browser runtime, credentials, or operator environment.

core.description: Pure default release-blocking checks; no mutation and no external provider dependency.

release.description: Full container release proof: core plus source immutability, hygiene, and deterministic build.

strict.description: Release proof plus advisory checks; warnings remain visible but do not block.

advisory.description: Non-blocking quality and ingestion warnings only.

local.description: Full release proof plus deployed Playwright click audit.

audit.description: Collect-all execution of every active and on-demand validator; local-only checks are deferred unless explicitly enabled.

social.description: Public-signal normalization and candidate loop validation.

llm.description: LLM export, answer-block, entity-graph, and citation-target validation.

homepages.description: Homepage-only schema and assistance boundary checks.

canonical-data.description: Protected canonical source static and runtime immutability checks.

postrelease.description: Pure post-build structural verification; no content release or mutation.

content-release.description: Lean content-release checks for generated static content and routing contracts.

agent-run.description: Agent artifact ingestion, FIX compilation, exact implementation, and semantic acceptance proof.

full-audit.description: Hostile collect-all review of all active validators without pretending every advisory check belongs in core.

citation-intelligence.description: Traffic-qualified citation intelligence, proof packet, atom, structural graph, and workflow topology gates.

deep-isolated.description: Isolated deep container validation: workflow data trace, browserless mock backup, and traffic-qualified citation intelligence only. No real browser claim.

HARD_FAIL.title: Canonical-data runtime immutability
HARD_FAIL.risk_prevented: A normal build could silently mutate protected canonical data.

HARD_FAIL.title: Canonical-data static write guard
HARD_FAIL.risk_prevented: Unapproved scripts could overwrite protected canonical source files.

HARD_FAIL.title: Canonical-domain contract and brand separation
HARD_FAIL.risk_prevented: Incorrect canonical routing can misdirect users and destroy citation attribution. Since 16 Oct 2026 it also fails if any canonical-domain href on an insights page is not in that canonical site's sitemap route list (data/canonical_route_snapshot.json, refreshed by scripts/refresh_canonical_route_snapshot.js), or if zero such links were checked. It also fails if any theindustryguides.com href on an insights page does not resolve to an ADMITTED (published) route, a static file or a _redirects source, or if zero internal links were checked. It also fails if any page URL in sitemap.xml or sitemaps/*.xml has no internal inbound link from another served page, if the homepage stops linking /insights/ and /atlas/, or if zero sitemap URLs were checked. Since 12 Oct 2026 it also fails if any built file in dist/ or any Pages Function source names Spry Labs, spryvc.com, joinwestpeek.com or westpeek.ventures, or if functions/api/request-assistance.js stops pinning the lead sender to The Industry Guides <hello@theindustryguides.com> (or reads env.EMAIL_FROM). Until then every lead email from theindustryguides.com went out From hello@joinwestpeek.com, hardcoded in wrangler.toml. Zero dist or function files scanned is a failure. wrangler.toml is out of scope by design: it carries the recipient (LEAD_TO), which no visitor sees.

HARD_FAIL.title: Content safety boundaries
HARD_FAIL.risk_prevented: Medical, legal, dental, immigration, or neuro content could cross advisory boundaries.

HARD_FAIL.title: Deep workflow command/data trace
HARD_FAIL.risk_prevented: Prevents workflow YAML commands from pointing at missing package scripts or missing command files during deep isolated validation.

HARD_FAIL.title: Build-result cache is byte-identical to a real build
HARD_FAIL.risk_prevented: A stale or corrupted cache entry restoring the wrong bytes onto a `npm run build:cached` no-op run - the entire 2,070-page site regenerated from scratch on every CI invocation was this repo's actual cost before this cache existed, and a cache that is fast but wrong is worse than no cache at all. This validator requires a cache entry for the CURRENT input hash, rejects one that never came from a completed build (readEntryMeta refuses a missing/false build_completed stamp or a mismatched input_hash before any file is touched), and then hashes every git-tracked file plus the cache-managed build dirs on both the current tree and an isolated, cache-disabled ground-truth rebuild - not a sample - and fails naming the exact files that differ.

HARD_FAIL.title: Primary-source and claim registry integrity, including retired authority URLs
HARD_FAIL.risk_prevented: Regulated or numeric pages could ship with missing, dangling, or malformed provenance records. ALSO PINS RETIRED AUTHORITY URLS (16 Oct 2026). Every state page cites a licensing board or a federal programme page by URL, and those publishers move pages without redirecting. Danielle's site-audit crawl of theindustryguides.com found nine such links serving 404 from live guide pages: the Montana, Iowa, South Dakota, Connecticut and Tennessee psychology boards, the Tennessee medical board, the CMS state-based exchange list, and the Georgia Medicaid dental fee schedule, whose quarterly PDF filename carries a publication timestamp GAMMIS rotates so a direct link rots within three months. A claim sourced to a dead URL is the root of a false public claim, which is this validator's own hard_fail_basis, so the pin lives here rather than as a forty-first blocker. scripts/lib/retired_authority_urls.js holds the retired/live pairs and the evidence for each; this validator calls it. It fails when a retired URL reappears in the evidence or page-family source files or in any rendered HTML, AND when a replacement URL is absent from the source files, which is what 'fixed to nothing' looks like. Deliberately offline: a live crawl in CI would go red on a publisher bot-blocking us (ftc.gov 404s its own root to this egress) or on a hosting outage (medicaid.ms.gov was serving a temporary-site notice on 2026-10-16); both were investigated on 16 Oct and left unpinned because neither was a defect on our side.

HARD_FAIL.title: MedicalWebPage and PriceSpecification are emitted and match the page
HARD_FAIL.risk_prevented: Prevents the medical schema types the citation runs asked for from being declared but not emitted, and prevents price markup quoting a figure the reader cannot see. content/_live/pages.json carried a schema_eligibility.medical_web_page flag on 220 records that no code path read.

HARD_FAIL.title: Published pages contain no internal build instructions
HARD_FAIL.risk_prevented: Agent recommendations are internal build directives shaped like 'FILEPATH: x || CURRENT: ... || EDIT: ...'. Two generator paths rendered them as reader-facing copy - a fallback acceptance-checklist card, and target.answer via 'Citation-ready update: '. 163 published pages carried the first and 100 the second, the latter inside the direct-answer block that answer engines extract. It also caused the external agent to re-flag pages marked released, because it was reading its own instruction back off the page.

HARD_FAIL.title: Occupancy measurement file may not shrink
HARD_FAIL.risk_prevented: Detects destruction of paid citation-occupancy measurements. On 2026-08-29 a scheduled run rewrote data/signals/query_class_occupancy.json without --merge and 205 recorded readings became 36: 170 grounded provider calls deleted by a run that exited 0 and reported success. The missing --merge was fixed the same day and the file was NOT rehydrated, because nothing in the repo knew how many readings there were supposed to be. This holds the expected depth outside the file, ratchets it upward only, and hard-fails when the measurement file falls below it or when a query that once carried a reading no longer does. A query may leave the panel only via an explicit retired_queries entry carrying a reason. Hard-fails on zero probes examined and on an empty high-water mark.

HARD_FAIL.title: Page record identity contract
HARD_FAIL.risk_prevented: Two records could claim one route, so a slug-keyed consumer picks a winner by iteration order and a repair script can write content into the empty record instead of the real page.

HARD_FAIL.title: Provider evidence contract validator
HARD_FAIL.risk_prevented: Prevents curated provider lists, review analysis, and unranked shortlists from claiming evidence that is missing, stale, unsupported, or not tied to a disclosed methodology.

HARD_FAIL.title: Public inventory contract
HARD_FAIL.risk_prevented: Unexpected, quarantined, or missing routes could enter the release.

HARD_FAIL.title: Release batch workflow contract
HARD_FAIL.risk_prevented: Batch mutation could bypass validation or push unsafe state.

HARD_FAIL.title: No page loses content without a named reason
HARD_FAIL.risk_prevented: Prevents a thaw-rebuild-reaccept cycle installing a thinner page as the new baseline. That is exactly how 14 KB and 22 KB of delivered content left two dentistry pages with CI green. Floors rise only; a page below its floor fails unless data/release/rendered_size_baseline.json names the shrink and the byte count it may fall to - a lowered floor, so a page that later grows above that size passes (2026-09-26, Validate Repo run 36225602982 went red on a page that had GAINED 634 bytes over its licence) and a page below it fails. A floor seeded today cannot see a page that was ALREADY re-frozen thinner - a sibling repo audited on the same day had 18 in that state - so data/release/historic_page_maximum.json enumerates this repo's 862 routes below their historic maximum (111 of which lost 626 delivered artifact blocks) as a shrink-only ratchet, and a new occurrence fails.

HARD_FAIL.title: Search Intelligence bounded self-healing and regulated-content safety
HARD_FAIL.risk_prevented: Prevents protected-path repair, regulated factual auto-repair, cooldown bypass, rollback without provenance, and no-op repairs counted as applied.

HARD_FAIL.title: No tracked file carries a git conflict marker
HARD_FAIL.risk_prevented: A tracked file could reach main carrying git conflict markers. On 2026-09-09 PRs #99, #100 and #101 were each rebased onto a main that had moved and the conflicts - all in regenerable validation receipts - were resolved with directory pathspecs (git checkout --theirs -- artifacts), which silently leaves any file git had already written markers into exactly as it found it. 28 receipts reached main corrupted, 828 marker lines in validation-summary-release.json alone. Nothing caught it: JSON with a conflict marker does not parse, so every reader fell into a catch and treated the file as ABSENT rather than corrupt - publish_gate_decision.mjs could not read the release summary at all. A corrupt receipt is worse than a missing one because it looks present. This scans every tracked text file for a marker at the start of a line.

HARD_FAIL.title: Validation severity policy self-test
HARD_FAIL.risk_prevented: A runner regression could silently treat a hard failure as a warning or turn advisory findings into false release blockers.

HARD_FAIL.title: Validation registry admission and matrix parity
HARD_FAIL.risk_prevented: Unregistered, duplicated, mutating, or misclassified validators can create false confidence and pipeline drift.

HARD_FAIL.title: Velocity commercial-intent page policy validator
HARD_FAIL.risk_prevented: Prevents best/top/comparison/review capture pages from shipping without Velocity-only separation, permitted ranking mode, disclosure, and evidence-backed methodology controls.

HARD_FAIL.title: GitHub Actions YAML syntax and top-level shape
HARD_FAIL.risk_prevented: A malformed workflow file can pass token-based trace checks but fail before any GitHub Actions job starts.

HARD_FAIL.title: Registered workflows and the scripts they run exist; GSC portfolio entry stays read-only
HARD_FAIL.risk_prevented: A workflow registered in data/workflows/workflow_contract_registry.json, or a script one of them runs, disappears from the tree, so a dispatch or schedule runs a command pointing at nothing. Also pins the GSC portfolio workflow's registry entry (read-only on the repo, modes matching the script) so a later build cannot drop it or turn it into a repo writer.

HARD_FAIL.title: Favicon, og:image, homepage JSON-LD, AEO definition + speakable, Clarity and IndexNow key stay in place
HARD_FAIL.risk_prevented: Measured 10 Oct 2026 on theindustryguides.com: /favicon.ico 404, no og:image on any page, no FAQPage or BreadcrumbList on the homepage and no definition paragraph for answer engines. Each item is registered in data/seo/site_hygiene_registry.json; this fails if a rebuild, content cycle or refactor drops any of them (files, build-chain step, homepage schema/definition/speakable, Clarity id, IndexNow key file).

HARD_FAIL.title: sameAs records satisfy the basis they claim
HARD_FAIL.risk_prevented: Identity claims made by resemblance: a VERIFIED sameAs that rests on no allowed basis, a third-party profile citing our own host, or a published sameAs that is not VERIFIED.

HARD_FAIL.title: No invented reviewers, providers, Person schema or sameAs
HARD_FAIL.risk_prevented: Invented people or medical/legal credential claims: reviewers, providers, Person schema and sameAs publishing without a VERIFIED record carrying an https credential or source URL; fabricated placeholder names; admitted pages without a visible byline and review date.

STRONG_WARNING.title: Lead submissions from BLOCKED_LEAD_DOMAINS are dropped quietly; all others are stored
STRONG_WARNING.risk_prevented: 26 Oct 2026 owner ruling: guide-site form submissions from blocked email domains (the BLOCKED_LEAD_DOMAINS Pages env var, comma-separated, never written in this repo) are dropped quietly - no Airtable write, no relay email, the honeypot's bare { ok: true }, one BLOCKED_LEAD log line. Fails when a blocked exact domain or subdomain reaches Airtable or Resend, when the response or log differs, or when an unlisted, look-alike or unset-env submission is not stored and relayed (a real lead silently lost).

STRONG_WARNING.title: The served tree keeps the head and disclosure contract: title 30-65, description 120-160 (fails only below 75% of a floor; over a ceiling never fails, the installer trims), complete social set, Organization with logo, ownership disclosure, capped link concentration
STRONG_WARNING.risk_prevented: Search Readiness audit of theindustryguides.com, 2026-10-25, measured in dist/: 414 titles over 65 characters, 1,327 meta descriptions over 160, 1,261 pages with no og:title, 1,262 without twitter:card summary_large_image, 2,137 with no common-ownership line and 2,137 with no Organization logo, plus one insight page linking a single canonical URL eight times (8 of 11 outbound links). 2,116 of the 2,136 admitted routes are frozen accepted bytes, so a generator-only fix cannot reach them; scripts/install_served_head_contract.js fixes them at publish time and this validator holds the result. It shares scripts/lib/served_head_contract.js with the installer, so the rule has one definition, and it refuses to pass having graded fewer than 1,500 pages.

STRONG_WARNING.title: Personal-injury legal copy never on a non-lawyer page (warning)
STRONG_WARNING.risk_prevented: Legal guidance (personal-injury rows) leaking onto dental, TRT, neuro or USCIS pages.

INFO.title: A fix recorded as released is shown by its page
INFO.risk_prevented: finalize_content_release.js marked a recommendation RELEASED_VERIFIED whenever its ROUTE completed a freeze transaction, which says nothing about whether the requested edit reached the page. Across the whole ledger 668 of 2,558 released claims were not shown by their pages. This fails if any fix claiming a released status is missing a required_marker from its rendered file.

Tier 4.title: The served tree keeps the head and disclosure contract: title 30-65, description 120-160 (fails only below 75% of a floor; over a ceiling never fails, the installer trims), complete social set, Organization with logo, ownership disclosure, capped link concentration
Tier 4.risk_prevented: Search Readiness audit of theindustryguides.com, 2026-10-25, measured in dist/: 414 titles over 65 characters, 1,327 meta descriptions over 160, 1,261 pages with no og:title, 1,262 without twitter:card summary_large_image, 2,137 with no common-ownership line and 2,137 with no Organization logo, plus one insight page linking a single canonical URL eight times (8 of 11 outbound links). 2,116 of the 2,136 admitted routes are frozen accepted bytes, so a generator-only fix cannot reach them; scripts/install_served_head_contract.js fixes them at publish time and this validator holds the result. It shares scripts/lib/served_head_contract.js with the installer, so the rule has one definition, and it refuses to pass having graded fewer than 1,500 pages.

Tier 7.title: No tracked file carries a git conflict marker
Tier 7.risk_prevented: A tracked file could reach main carrying git conflict markers. On 2026-09-09 PRs #99, #100 and #101 were each rebased onto a main that had moved and the conflicts - all in regenerable validation receipts - were resolved with directory pathspecs (git checkout --theirs -- artifacts), which silently leaves any file git had already written markers into exactly as it found it. 28 receipts reached main corrupted, 828 marker lines in validation-summary-release.json alone. Nothing caught it: JSON with a conflict marker does not parse, so every reader fell into a catch and treated the file as ABSENT rather than corrupt - publish_gate_decision.mjs could not read the release summary at all. A corrupt receipt is worse than a missing one because it looks present. This scans every tracked text file for a marker at the start of a line.
